learningObjective: Master the crucial architectural distinction in SAP GTS between Sanctioned Party List (SPL) screening (WHO is involved) and Product Export Control / SCOMET classification (WHAT is being exported).
commonMistake: Searching DGFT SCOMET lists in SPL screening engines. SCOMET is a dual-use technical goods classification, not a denied persons list.
interviewExplanation: In SAP GTS, Trade Compliance is divided into SPL Screening (/SAPSLL/SPL_CHCK) and Legal Control / Export Licenses (/SAPSLL/LIC_MGMT). SCOMET, EAR99, and ITAR classify products via Export Control Classification Numbers (ECCNs). A clean partner can still be blocked if the material requires a government export license.
consultantNote: Never combine SCOMET product control data with sanctioned party screening. SCOMET determines whether an export license is legally mandated based on item capability and destination country.

explanationPanel.whatIsHappening: Customer 'NEXUS TRAINING PARTNER 999' is completely clean on sanctions lists. However, document NX-SO-800011 is held under Export Control because material NX-MAT-100003 is classified under DGFT SCOMET Category 8A102.
explanationPanel.whyGtsPerformsCheck: DGFT regulations mandate government export authorizations for dual-use strategic goods to prevent illicit technology proliferation.
